title: Law Firm Operating Accounts Outside the IOLTA (2026)
summary: Client trust money stays in an IOLTA. See what goes in a law firm's operating account, and how Slash, Novo, Mercury, Ramp, and Chase handle it.
body_markdown:
****


## What Slash Does For a Law Firm’s Operating Account


For most law firms, client trust money stays in an IOLTA at a bank your state bar lists as eligible, and the operating account sits beside it. Retainers that haven’t been earned, client cost advances, and settlement funds all belong there. The operating account, meanwhile, holds the firm's own money: fees once earned and transferred out of trust, payroll, rent, software, and the case costs the firm pays before billing them.


Slash, a[business banking platform](https://www.slash.com/products/business-banking) ¹ for US companies, covers the operating side. Its eligibility rules bar using an account to hold money on behalf of clients or other third parties, so it’s not where you’ll put a retainer or a settlement. Below, we take a look at what belongs on each side of the line, then how Slash, Novo, Mercury, Ramp, and Chase handle the operating account.


### Key Takeaways


- ABA Model Rule 1.15 puts fees and expenses paid in advance into a client trust account, to be withdrawn only as the lawyer earns the fees or incurs the expenses.
- Slash lists law firms among the businesses it supports, and its eligibility rules bar holding funds for third parties. A firm can use it as the operating account while keeping the IOLTA elsewhere.
- Slash issues virtual cards on both plans, Free at $0 and Pro from $25 a month, so a firm can give each matter its own card with merchant category limits.
- Novo says it doesn’t offer IOLTA accounts, and Mercury's deposit agreement with Choice Financial Group bars IOLTA funds.
- Ramp asks for $25,000 in a linked US business bank account before you apply, and its Operating Account is not available to businesses based in New York or Hawaii.


## What Belongs in a Law Firm's Operating Account Instead of the IOLTA?


The line follows who owns the money. Under[ABA Model Rule 1.15](https://www.americanbar.org/groups/professional_responsibility/publications/model_rules_of_professional_conduct/rule_1_15_safekeeping_property/) , legal fees and expenses paid in advance go into the client trust account and come out only as they’re earned or incurred. A lawyer can put firm money into trust only to cover the trust account's own bank charges, and the rule keeps the lawyer's own property separate from client property. Earned fees therefore move out of trust to the operating account instead of staying in the IOLTA. The ABA's[Formal Opinion 505](https://www.americanbar.org/content/dam/aba/administrative/professional_responsibility/ethics-opinions/aba-formal-opinion-505.pdf) adds that calling an advance "earned upon receipt" or "nonrefundable" does not make it earned.


The bank holding the IOLTA is a separate decision. In California, a lawyer can open an IOLTA only at an institution on the State Bar's[list of IOLTA-eligible financial institutions](https://www.calbar.ca.gov/access-justice/financial-institutions-banking-compliance/iolta-eligible-financial-institutions) , and the account name has to include "IOLTA," "trust account," or similar wording. Since 2026, California also requires banks to report every attorney trust account to the State Bar each year. Other states run their own lists, so check yours before you choose a bank for trust money.


Everything the firm owns outright goes through the operating account. Earned fees arrive there from trust by ACH or wire, and payroll, rent, malpractice premiums, software, and the filing fees the firm fronts leave from it. These are the criteria the ranking uses:


- **Earned fees in by ACH or wire:** US account and routing numbers that accept the transfer out of trust once a bill is paid.
- **Cards per matter:** A card for each matter or practice group, limited by merchant category, so case costs are easy to bill back.
- **Separate buckets for firm money:** Places to hold payroll, tax set-asides, and partner distributions apart from day-to-day spending.
- **Approvals on payments out:** Rules that hold a large payment until a second person signs off.
- **Ledger sync:** Coded transactions flowing to QuickBooks Online, Xero, Sage Intacct, or NetSuite.


## 1. Slash: Per-Matter Cards, Separate Buckets, and Two-Way Ledger Sync


Slash's[FAQ](https://www.slash.com/faq) lists law firms alongside consultants and professional services as generally supported, with eligibility decided case by case. Its[eligibility page](https://www.slash.com/help-center/getting-started/how-to-know-if-you-re-eligible-for-slash) says "Slash is unable to support businesses that intend to use Slash accounts to receive, hold, move, or distribute funds on behalf of customers, users, players, or other third parties." A firm uses Slash for money it has already earned, and deposits are FDIC-insured² up to $200 million through a sweep network of partner banks.


### What Slash Does for a Law Firm's Operating Account


- **Earned fees by ACH or wire:** Once a fee is earned, the firm sends it from the IOLTA to its Slash account and routing numbers, which take incoming ACH and wire transfers.
- [Virtual cards](https://www.slash.com/products/corporate-cards) :You can issue one card for each matter, so filing fees, court reporters, and records requests for that matter post to its own card. Physical cards are available for any team member.
- [Merchant category controls](https://www.slash.com/help-center/corporate-cards/configuring-spend-limits-on-your-slash-cards) : Each card can allow or block merchant categories, MCC codes, specific merchants, and countries, all with transaction and spending limits.
- [Virtual accounts](https://www.slash.com/help-center/business-banking/creating-and-managing-virtual-accounts) : An Owner or Admin creates as many as the firm needs, each with its own account and routing numbers, for things like tax set-asides and partner distributions.
- [Payment policies](https://www.slash.com/help-center/account-management/configuring-outgoing-transfer-approval-controls) : A policy checks each outgoing payment by amount, by who requested it, or both, then sends it to an approval chain of one or more named people or roles.
- [Two-way accounting sync](https://www.slash.com/platform/accounting) : Slash imports the chart of accounts and other reference data from QuickBooks Online, Xero, Sage Intacct, and NetSuite and sends coded transactions back.


Expert witnesses and court reporters can be paid through[Bill Pay](https://www.slash.com/products/bill-pay) , where a forwarded or uploaded invoice becomes a bill and waits for its approvers before payment.


### What It Costs


Free costs $0 a month and pays a default[1.5% cashback](https://www.slash.com/help-center/corporate-cards/understanding-slash-cashback) on eligible purchases with the Slash Visa® Platinum Card. Pro starts at $25 a month, pays up to 2%, and charges $0 for same-day ACH, domestic wires, and outgoing FedNow and RTP payments.


The[pricing page](https://www.slash.com/pricing) lists $1 per same-day ACH payment and $6 per domestic wire on Free. Virtual cards, virtual accounts, and merchant controls come with both plans, so the plan choice turns on how many wires and same-day payments the firm sends.


## 2. Novo: A $0 Operating Account That Takes No Cash and Holds No IOLTA


Novo runs a[page for law offices](https://www.novo.co/industries/law-practice-legal-services) that offers business checking with no monthly fee and no minimum balance, plus branded invoices paid through Stripe or Square. It connects to QuickBooks, Xero, and Wave, and its Reserves feature sets money aside for taxes. Novo allows no more than 20 Reserves, and they have no account numbers of their own. Banking is provided by Middlesex Federal Savings, F.A.


Novo's[guide for solo practice lawyers](https://www.novo.co/business-expenses/lawyers-solo-practice) says Novo does not offer IOLTA trust accounts and recommends pairing it with an IOLTA at a state-approved bank. It also says Novo does not accept cash deposits, so a firm that takes cash retainers keeps a second account at an institution that does. Novo accepts sole proprietorships, LLCs, partnerships, and corporations.


## 3. Mercury: Law Firms in Its FAQ, IOLTA Funds Barred by Its Deposit Agreement


Mercury's[FAQ](https://mercury.com/faq) names law firms among the businesses it serves, and its help center lists LLPs among the company structures it supports. The[commercial deposit account agreement](https://mercury.com/legal/choice/commercial-deposit-account-agreement) with Choice Financial Group, one of Mercury's partner banks, bars the account from holding IOLA or IOLTA client trust funds and qualified settlement funds.


On the operating side, Mercury's[pricing page](https://mercury.com/pricing) lists $0, Plus at $29.90, and Pro at $299 a month, billed annually. Mercury issues as many virtual cards as a business needs, offers category-locked cards, and publishes up to 100 checking and 100 savings accounts per business. It connects to QuickBooks Online, Xero, and NetSuite, but not Sage Intacct. FDIC coverage runs up to $5 million through its partner banks and their sweep networks.


## 4. Ramp: $25,000 in a Linked Bank Account to Apply, and an Operating Account for Firm Expenses


Ramp's[legal industry page](https://ramp.com/industry/legal) says it manages firm operating expenses only and does not replace IOLTA trust accounting software, and it suggests one virtual card per client matter. Ramp also publishes a guide for law firms, “What Is IOLTA?”, dated June 7, 2026.


The[Ramp Operating Account](https://support.ramp.com/ramp-operating-account-overview) is a pooled account at JPMorgan Chase, where Ramp Payments Corp holds the funds on the customer's behalf with pass-through FDIC coverage. Businesses based in New York or Hawaii cannot open it and are offered the Ramp Checking Account at First Internet Bank of Indiana instead.


To apply, Ramp's[qualifications](https://support.ramp.com/applying-and-signing-up-for-ramp-us-based) call for a US corporation, LLC, or LP with at least $25,000 in cash in a linked US business bank account, and Ramp does not accept sole proprietors. The free plan connects QuickBooks Online and Xero, and NetSuite and Sage Intacct need Ramp Plus at $15 a user a month plus a platform fee.


## 5. Chase: Business Complete Banking at $15 a Month, With Attorney Trust Accounts in the Same Agreement


[Business Complete Banking](https://www.chase.com/business/banking/checking/business-complete-banking) costs $15 a month. Chase waives the fee for a $2,000 minimum daily ending balance, $2,000 in Chase Payment Solutions deposits, $2,000 in purchases on a linked Chase business credit card, or a linked Chase Private Client account. Opening takes no minimum deposit, and a new customer funds the account within 60 days.


Chase's[deposit account agreement](https://www.chase.com/content/dam/chase-ux/documents/personal/checking/deposit-account-agreement.pdf) covers attorney trust accounts, including IOLTAs, and lets Chase notify the state agency when one is overdrawn or a check is dishonored where state rules require it. A firm can ask a Chase banker about holding the operating account and the IOLTA at one bank, after checking that Chase is on its state's eligible list.

## How to Choose an Operating Account for a Law Firm


- **Open the IOLTA first:** Pick a bank on your state bar's eligible list, then choose the operating account around it, since the operating account can sit anywhere.
- **Trace how earned fees leave trust:** Your trust accounting software or bank sends them by ACH or wire, so you’ll want to confirm the operating account takes both and shows who sent each deposit.
- **Give each matter its own card:** Costs billed back to a client are easier to support when every charge for that matter lives on the same card. Check the card count and the merchant controls before you issue them.
- **Price the transfers you send:** A firm sending 15 domestic wires and 25 same-day ACH payments a month pays $90 plus $25, or $115, on Slash Free and $0 on Pro from $25 a month. Chase's $15 fee comes to $180 a year unless a waiver applies.
- **Match the sync to your ledger:** A firm on Sage Intacct or NetSuite narrows the list, so be sure to check integrations before making your pick.


## Running the Operating Side in Slash


1. Share the Slash account and routing numbers from Entity Documents with whoever releases earned fees from the IOLTA.
2. Create virtual accounts for payroll, tax set-asides, and partner distributions, and move money into them from the main account.
3. Issue a virtual card for each active matter, and put them in a card group with merchant category limits.
4. Set a payment policy so payments above an amount you choose wait for a second approver.
5. Connect QuickBooks Online, Xero, Sage Intacct, or NetSuite so coded transactions reach the ledger.


## Conclusion


Novo allows no more than 20 Reserves without their own account numbers, Mercury names no Sage Intacct integration, Ramp asks for $25,000 in a linked account before it opens, and Chase charges $15 a month unless a waiver applies.


Slash runs the firm's earned money with a card for every matter, uncapped virtual accounts for payroll and taxes, approvals on payments out, and two-way sync with all four major ledgers, all while the IOLTA stays at a bank your state bar lists as eligible.


Talk to the Slash team about[running your firm's operating account and matter cards on Slash](https://www.slash.com/sales-inquiry) .


## FAQs


### 1. Can a law firm use Slash as its IOLTA?


No. Slash's eligibility rules bar firms from using an account to receive or hold funds on behalf of clients or other third parties. Client trust money stays in an IOLTA at a bank your state bar lists as eligible.


### 2. Does Slash work with law firms?


Slash's FAQ lists law firms among the businesses it generally supports, alongside consultants and professional services. Eligibility is reviewed case by case, based on the firm's activities, ownership, jurisdiction, and the products it asks for.


### 3. How do earned fees get from the IOLTA into Slash?


By ACH or wire, once the fee is earned. The firm's trust account sends the transfer to the Slash account and routing numbers, which are listed in Entity Documents along with a downloadable bank letter.


### 4. Can a firm track case costs by matter in Slash?


Yes. Slash issues virtual cards on both plans, so each matter can have its own card with merchant category limits. Coded transactions then sync two-way with QuickBooks Online, Xero, Sage Intacct, or NetSuite.


### 5. What money belongs in a law firm's operating account?


Money the firm has earned or owns outright. That covers fees after they are earned and moved out of trust, payroll, rent, software, insurance, and case costs the firm pays before billing them. Advance fees, client cost advances, and settlement funds stay in trust.
